facts.value: A negative incoming result enters terminal handling without checking cancellation. For a nonnegative result, negative fileInfo->length produces CARD_RESULT_CANCELED before accounting for the completed sector; otherwise sectorSize is deducted. A positive remainder advances offset and follows the FAT, rejecting a next block below 5 or at least card->cBlock with CARD_RESULT_BROKEN, then starts the next erase. A nonpositive remainder updates the directory timestamp, captures apiCallback, clears that field, and passes the captured callback to __CARDUpdateDir. Accepted erase or directory startup leaves completion pending. Ordinary terminal handling captures and clears apiCallback, releases control, asserts the callback exists, and invokes it. Exceptional directory-start failure reaches that same terminal label after apiCallback has already been cleared: it reloads NULL rather than the previously captured callback. __CARDUpdateDir can fail immediately without restoring apiCallback, so this branch must not be described as guaranteed normal callback notification. Accepted directory persistence instead stores the handed-off callback in eraseCallback and completes through the directory layer.
facts.rationale: Preserves the supported result, cancellation, length and FAT transitions while adding the previously omitted callback-ownership exception visible across CARDWrite and CARDDir.

evidence.why: Shows cancellation precedence, countdown, FAT checks, callback clearing before directory startup, and terminal reload.
Shows immediate no-card failure and callback storage in eraseCallback rather than restoration of apiCallback.
Shows directory completion's control release and transferred callback notification.
